items.statement: Where residual solvent levels above the guideline limits are used (e.g. short-term use of 30 days or less, or topical application), justify those higher levels case by case.
items.quote:
Higher levels of residual
solvents may be acceptable in certain cases such as short term (30 days or less) or topical
application. Justification for these levels should be made on a case by case basis.

items.statement: Identify and quantify Class 1 solvents whenever they are likely to be present.
items.quote: If Class 1 solvents are likely to be present, they should be identified and quantified.

items.statement: Identify and quantify Class 2 solvents present above their Option 1 limits and Class 3 solvents present above 0.5%.
items.quote:
If solvents of Class 2 or Class 3 are present at greater than their Option 1 limits or 0.5%,
respectively, they should be identified and quantified.
items.condition: Class 2 above Option 1 limit or Class 3 above 0.5%

items.statement: Do not use Class 1 solvents in manufacturing drug substances, excipients or drug products.
items.quote:
Solvents in Class 1 should not be employed in the manufacture of drug substances, excipients, and
drug products because of their unacceptable toxicity or their deleterious environmental effect.

items.statement: Where Class 1 solvent use cannot be avoided to make a drug product with a significant therapeutic advance, restrict their levels to the Table 1 limits unless otherwise justified.
items.quote:
However, if their use is unavoidable in order to produce a drug product with a significant
therapeutic advance, then their levels should be restricted as shown in Table 1, unless otherwise
justified.
items.condition: Class 1 use unavoidable for significant therapeutic advance; unless otherwise justified

items.statement: Where Benzene (Class 1) is used, keep its residual level at or below 2 ppm.
Where Carbon tetrachloride (Class 1) is used, keep its residual level at or below 4 ppm.
items.quote: Carbon tetrachloride | 4 | Toxic and environmental hazard

items.statement: Where 1,2-Dichloroethane (Class 1) is used, keep its residual level at or below 5 ppm.
Where 1,1-Dichloroethene (Class 1) is used, keep its residual level at or below 8 ppm.
Where 1,1,1-Trichloroethane (Class 1) is used, keep its residual level at or below 1500 ppm.

not_applicable.text: "Likely to be present" refers to the solvent used in the final manufacturing step
1,1,1-Trichloroethane is included in Table 1 because it is an environmental hazard.
The stated limit of 1500 ppm is based on a review of the safety data.

items.statement: Limit the Class 2 solvents listed in Table 2 in pharmaceutical products.
items.quote:
Solvents in Table 2 should be limited in pharmaceutical products because of their inherent
toxicity.

items.statement: Determine the analytical precision for residual solvent testing as part of method validation.
items.quote: Precision should be determined as part of the validation of the method.

It is considered that amounts of these residual solvents of 50
mg per day or less (corresponding to 5000 ppm or 0.5% under Option 1) would be acceptable

items.statement: Class 3 residual solvent amounts above 50 mg per day may be accepted only if they are realistic for manufacturing capability and good manufacturing practice.
items.quote:
Higher amounts may also be acceptable provided they are realistic in relation
to manufacturing capability and good manufacturing practice.
items.condition: provided realistic for manufacturing capability and GMP
